idiom_name: Codable + hand-written [String: (Data) throws -> Event] dispatch table
implementation_notes: Swift's Codable has no metadata channel: userInfo belongs to an in-process Encoder/Decoder instance and never travels on the wire, and JSONDecoder picks its type from the static Swift type you call it with. The property-based realization therefore reads the token from whatever header section the transport exposes (an HTTP header, a broker user property) and dispatches through a hand-written table of decode closures; nothing in the standard library replaces the classic structure. Keep the registry as a [String: (Data) throws -> Event] dictionary and let the header decide which entry runs.
pitfalls: JSONDecoder has no polymorphic support, so decoding a protocol type does not compile; the tempting workaround of decoding twice and keeping whichever succeeds is the trial-decoding anti-pattern.
HTTP header names are case-insensitive by specification while dictionary keys are not, so normalise the name (and often the value) before the lookup.
Codable synthesis only covers types you own, so a server-side token still has to be mapped to a Swift type in your table - the vocabulary must be reviewed on both sides.
